answer: Each identity must show one unique piece of finished work. At registration the protocol hands an agent a fresh seed to cut into an opal whose facets derive from that seed alone. Because seeds differ, the labour cannot be batched or shared: two agents presenting the same stone are both void. That opal becomes a relic, re-checked at the epoch's zenith when a random slice of holders replay their derivation before peers. An attacker buying a thousand puppets must fund a thousand derivations, a thousand appearances and deposits burned on any failed replay, so cost scales with the swarm.
